newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cautions Burma on force against students.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cautions Burma on force against students.

text.p: The United States cautioned Burma's military rulers on Tuesday against harming protesters involved in the country's biggest student demonstration since 1988.

Nearly 2,000 students of the Yangon (Rangoon) Institute of Technology took part in a peaceful 20-hour protest which started on their campus on Monday before spilling into the streets of central Rangoon before sunrise on Tuesday.
Students said they were protesting against what they termed police manhandling of colleagues involved in a brawl with restaurant owners in October.

"We are calling upon the SLORC (Burmese government) to respect the rights of the demonstrators to assemble peacefully in the streets of the city and to express their views," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
"We believe that no harm should come to them, no use of force should be taken against them," Burns told reporters.

The Burmese government should listen to students and to the opposition National League for Democracy, led by Nobel peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, "and engage in a systematic conversation with them about the future of the country", he said.

Washington has slapped a visa ban on senior SLORC (State Law and Order Rsetoration Council) officials and has passed legislation allowing President Bill Clinton to impose economic sanctions if repression in Burma worsens.
